title: Computational Practice
subtitle: Computational design seminar
summary: A large-format seminar connecting parametric modeling, geometry, materiality, and digital fabrication through architectural applications.
body: The course followed a dual trajectory of parametric facades and minimal surfaces, advancing from precedent analysis and geometric variation toward form finding, mesh modeling, physics-based simulation, fabrication, and installation-scale assembly.

Twelve weekly exercises and two major group projects created a scaffolded learning sequence. Approximately thirty percent of class time was dedicated to lectures and demonstrations, while seventy percent operated as an open workshop supported by tutorials, templates, scripts, and teaching assistants.

Three instructional sequences structured the semester: Parametric Facades, a Generative AI Workshop, and Minimal Surfaces. Students moved from rule-based facade systems to AI-assisted visualization and then to topology, mesh segmentation, joinery, fabrication, and collective construction.

The final work connected screen-based exploration to material practice through precedent studies, variation matrices, form-finding models, fabrication diagrams, mock-ups, and installation-scale assemblies.
